fixes.explanation: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, writes that these exiles were "…sanctified by the Spirit for obedience to Jesus Christ…" (1 Peter 1:2). Look at who shows up in that one verse: God the Father, the Spirit and Jesus Christ. Peter puts all three right there in his greeting. Good work, friend.

Peter doesn't list those here. He says the Spirit of Christ in the prophets "…predicted the sufferings of Christ and the glories to follow." (1 Peter 1:11). Two things, friend: the sufferings, then the glories. Birth and baptism aren't in that verse.

Yes, them. Peter says it was revealed to the prophets "…that they were not serving themselves, but you…" (1 Peter 1:12). The "you" is the folks reading his letter. Those prophets searched and investigated carefully, and they were serving Peter's readers all along. I feel that in my mustache.

True. The last line of the passage says, "Even angels long to look into these things." (1 Peter 1:12). Angels, friend. Peter says they long to look into the very things the gospel preachers announced. I think that makes the good news pretty special.
